title: Cross‑SDK transport operating guidance: timeouts, pools, keep‑alive, and streaming ergonomics
text:
Cross‑SDK transport operating guidance: timeouts, pools, keep‑alive, and streaming ergonomics

description:
Objective: produce a single, language-idiomatic set of recommended transport defaults and examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that optimize for low-latency request/response, robust streaming, and predictable unit economics. Deliverables: (1) concrete default presets for connect/read/write/idle timeouts, pool sizing, and keep-alive settings per language; (2) streaming ergonomics patterns including backpressure, cancellation, and partial-result handling; (3) retry guidance aligned to idempotency and streaming semantics; (4) cookbook examples and test harnesses; (5) documentation pages and code samples for quick adoption by app developers and platform teams.

acceptance_criteria:
Language-specific presets exist for Python, TypeScript, and Go and are included in each SDK's default transport config.
Cookbook contains at least three real-world examples: low-latency interactive chat, high-throughput batched embeddings, and long-running server-side streaming.
Automated unit and integration tests validate timeouts, pool exhaustion behavior, and streaming cancelation across CI networks.
Benchmarks show no regression in median latency and improved P95 behavior under connection churn compared to current defaults.
Docs page with clear migration notes and a one-line opt-in for legacy behavior is published.
PRs for Python/TS/Go SDKs merged with opt-in presets and feature flags behind a config toggle for rollout.
Telemetry events emitted for pool saturation, keepalive failures, and streaming reconnects to feed Optimize recommendations.

technical_notes:
Recommended baseline values (starting point to tune per workload): connect_timeout=3s, request_timeout=60s for non-streaming, initial_stream_read_timeout=120s with active keepalive pings every 30s; idle_conn_timeout=90s; max_idle_conns=100 per CPU for server-side workers; http2/keepalive probes enabled where supported.
Python notes: for sync/requests-based wrappers use urllib3 PoolManager with maxsize tuned to min(32, cpu_count*8); for async use httpx.AsyncClient with limits=Limits(max_keepalive_connections=100, max_connections=200) and http2 enabled for streaming. Use asyncio shielded cancelation with explicit stream.close() to avoid leaked tasks.
TypeScript notes: for browser SDKs rely on fetch streaming semantics; for Node use undici or native http.Agent with keepAlive=true, keepAliveMsecs=30000, maxSockets per agent = cpu_count*16 or configurable via SDK constructor. Provide example Agent presets and show how to attach signal for AbortController to cancel streaming fetches cleanly.
Go notes: recommend http.Transport tweaks: MaxIdleConns=200, MaxIdleConnsPerHost=100, IdleConnTimeout=90s, TLSHandshakeTimeout=5s, ExpectContinueTimeout=1s. Use context.Context timeouts for per-request cancelation and small buffer sizes on streaming readers to reduce memory spikes.
Streaming ergonomics: expose a stable iterator/async iterator pattern across SDKs with early-cancel helpers, heartbeat/keepalive hooks, and an opt-in automatic reconnect for idempotent stream restarts. For non-idempotent streams, offer checkpointing + explicit resume API that SDKs surface in examples.
Retry strategy: use conservative automatic retries for idempotent unary calls (up to 2 retries with exponential backoff starting at 200ms) and NO automatic retry for non-idempotent streaming requests. Provide opt-in retry middleware that integrates with SDK backpressure signals.
Observability: emit structured events for connection pool saturation, request timeout, idle-connection-reaped, stream-cancel, and stream-heartbeat-missed with consistent naming across SDKs for Console and Optimize ingestion.
Config model: SDKs should expose a small POSIX-like preset set (low-latency, balanced, high-throughput) and allow explicit per-client override. Provide migration path where old flat timeout options map to new preset model.
Interop constraints: where underlying runtime lacks keepalive probes (some browsers), provide JS-only soft-heartbeat that sends application-level no-op frames when policy allows.

decisions:
Adopt a preset model (low-latency, balanced, throughput) rather than a one-size-fits-all default to simplify user choices and enable clear docs.
Limit automatic retries to idempotent unary endpoints. Streaming auto-reconnect will be opt-in and explicit.
Expose a single cross-SDK telemetry event taxonomy for transport-level incidents to simplify Console ingestion and Optimize analysis.
Implement language-specific examples rather than forcing identical code shapes across SDKs; however keep API surface analogous (sync/async iterator patterns).

action_items:
Spike: run microbenchmarks for default presets on representative cloud VMs and measure P50/P95/P99 for short-chat and long-stream workloads (owner: Marco).
Author initial cookbook draft with three examples and per-language snippets (owner: Aisha).
Implement config presets and telemetry hooks in Python SDK PR (owner: Priya Shah).
Implement Node/undici and browser examples, add AbortController cancelation pattern to TS SDK (owner: Leo Chen).
Implement Go Transport presets and streaming iterator with context cancellation (owner: Diego Ruiz).
Add CI integration tests simulating pool exhaustion and slow networks using tox/dockerized chaos tests (owner: SRE).
Coordinate with Console team to ensure telemetry mapping and dashboard widgets for pool/keepalive metrics (owner: Marco).

test_plan:
Unit tests cover preset parsing and fallback behavior for missing fields.
Integration tests simulate 1000 concurrent clients with aggressive connect/disconnect cycles to ensure no file descriptor leaks and acceptable latency tail behavior.
Streaming tests validate graceful cancelation, no goroutine/task leaks, and client-visible error codes for reconnect vs user-cancel.
Chaos test: inject delayed TCP handshakes and dropped packets to validate backoff and pool exhaustion handling.
Telemetry test: synthetic scenario that triggers pool-saturation event and verifies Console ingestion and alert firing.
Performance regression: compare median and P95 latency against baseline (current defaults) and require no worse than 10% regression on median for balanced preset.

rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): merge presets behind feature flag; opt-in customers only. Monitor telemetry for 48h.
Phase 2 (gradual): enable default for SDK minor release for 10% of new sessions; observe pool saturation and streaming errors; rollback toggle if alerts breach thresholds.
Phase 3 (general): enable by default in next minor release after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and docs updates.
Provide migration note and one-line opt-out config for customers who need old behavior.
Coordinate with Customer Success to reach out to top 20 Dedicated/Enterprise customers for early testing and feedback.
